title: Bodies, Fairness, Safety & Friendship

myths.myth: Boys' and girls' bodies are completely different in every way.
myths.truth: Most of our bodies are the same; only a few parts differ.
myths.explanation: Hearts, lungs, bones, brains: all the same. Every body is amazing.

myths.myth: It's rude to ask how bodies work.
myths.truth: Curiosity about your body is good and normal.
myths.explanation: Asking a trusted grown-up is the smart thing to do.

myths.myth: Your body stays the same forever.
myths.truth: Bodies grow and change as you get older.
myths.explanation: Growing up is normal and happens at everyone's own pace.

myths.myth: Some bodies are better than others.
myths.truth: All bodies are good bodies.
myths.explanation: Bodies come in all shapes, sizes, colours and abilities.

myths.myth: Being a boy or girl is about what you like (toys, clothes).
myths.truth: Who you are is much more than that, and likes don't have a gender.
myths.explanation: You can be you, however you like.

myths.myth: Boys must act one way and girls another.
myths.truth: There's no one way to be a boy or a girl.
myths.explanation: Be yourself; everyone's different.

myths.myth: You can tell everything about someone from boy or girl.
myths.truth: Everyone is their own unique person.
myths.explanation: Gender doesn't decide who you are inside.

myths.myth: Liking 'opposite' things means something's wrong.
myths.truth: Liking all kinds of things is normal and great.
myths.explanation: Your interests are yours.

myths.myth: You must do whatever any grown-up says, always.
myths.truth: Safe grown-ups won't ask for unsafe or secret things. You can say no.
myths.explanation: Your safety rules still count, even with adults.

myths.myth: Telling on someone who hurt you is being a tattletale.
myths.truth: Telling a trusted adult about unsafe things is brave and right.
myths.explanation: That's not tattling. It's keeping safe.

myths.myth: If you didn't say no, it's your fault.
myths.truth: Unsafe touch is never your fault.
myths.explanation: The grown-up who does it is responsible, always.

myths.myth: Everyone online is who they say they are.
myths.truth: People online aren't always who they claim.
myths.explanation: Don't share private info; tell a trusted adult if something feels off.

myths.myth: Keep scary online things a secret.
myths.truth: Tell a trusted grown-up about anything online that worries you.
myths.explanation: A safe adult will help; you won't be in trouble.

myths.myth: If someone's mean sometimes, you must stay best friends.
myths.truth: A good friend treats you kindly; you don't have to stay where you're treated badly.
myths.explanation: Friendship should feel good more than it hurts.

myths.myth: Friends should do everything you say (or you, theirs).
myths.truth: Good friends respect each other; you can say no.
myths.explanation: Real friends don't pressure you.

myths.myth: You can only have one best friend.
myths.truth: You can have many friends, in many ways.
myths.explanation: There's room for lots of friendship.

myths.myth: Saying sorry means you lost.
myths.truth: Saying sorry and making up makes friendships stronger.
myths.explanation: Everyone has squabbles; repairing them is what counts.

myths.myth: Being left out is something to just put up with.
myths.truth: Including others is kind; if you're left out, tell someone and find kind friends.
myths.explanation: No one should be left out for being different.

myths.myth: Boys should get to go first or lead.
myths.truth: Everyone gets a fair turn.
myths.explanation: Fairness means equal chances for all.

myths.myth: Cooking and cleaning are girls' / mum's job.
myths.truth: Everyone shares the chores.
myths.explanation: Chores aren't girls' or boys' work.

myths.myth: Some kids deserve more than others.
myths.truth: Everyone deserves fairness and respect.
myths.explanation: All children have the same rights.

myths.myth: It's okay to leave someone out for being different.
myths.truth: Everyone should get to join in.
myths.explanation: Including everyone is what fair play means.

myths.myth: Winning is all that matters.
myths.truth: Playing fair and being kind matter most.
myths.explanation: How you play matters more than the score.

myths.myth: Teasing a 'girly boy' or 'tomboy' is just a joke.
myths.truth: Teasing about gender isn't funny. It hurts.
myths.explanation: Jokes that put people down aren't kind.

myths.myth: 'Boys will be boys', so it's okay.
myths.truth: Being unkind is never okay, for anyone.
myths.explanation: No one gets a pass to be mean.

myths.myth: If it's not happening to you, it's not your problem.
myths.truth: You can be an ally: speak up or get help when someone's teased.
myths.explanation: Standing up safely helps everyone.

myths.myth: Laughing along makes you cool.
myths.truth: Being kind makes you a good friend.
myths.explanation: Kindness is the cool thing.

myths.myth: Everything on screens is real and true.
myths.truth: Lots of what we see is pretend or made up.
myths.explanation: Cartoons, ads and edited pictures aren't real life.

myths.myth: If it's on a screen, you should believe it.
myths.truth: It's smart to ask 'is this real?'
myths.explanation: Check with a grown-up when you're not sure.

myths.myth: Ads just tell you the truth about toys and snacks.
myths.truth: Ads try to make you want things. They don't tell the whole truth.
myths.explanation: Knowing the trick means it can't fool you.

myths.myth: It's fine to share photos or info with anyone online.
myths.truth: Keep private things private; ask a trusted adult.
myths.explanation: Online, not everyone is a friend.

myths.myth: More screen time is always better.
myths.truth: Screens are fun in balance.
myths.explanation: Play, rest and people matter too.

myths.myth: If you're upset, just snap out of it.
myths.truth: Big feelings calm in small steps.
myths.explanation: Breathe, count, take space, talk to someone.

myths.myth: You can't tell how someone else feels.
myths.truth: You can notice feelings in faces, bodies and words.
myths.explanation: Noticing others is called empathy.

myths.myth: Being kind is for pushovers.
myths.truth: Kindness is a strength.
myths.explanation: It takes courage to be kind.

myths.myth: When you're angry, it's okay to hit or yell.
myths.truth: All feelings are okay; hurting others is not.
myths.explanation: Use words, take a break, ask for help.
